scenes.title: Master Summary: Contracts, Hedging, and Systemic Safety

beatOutlines.textOutline: Review of the 8 core principles from standardized futures to systemic contagion and regulatory clearing.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: 1. Futures contracts are standardized, binding agreements traded on organized exchanges for future delivery at a set price [fact-01].
2. Forward contracts provide over-the-counter equivalents negotiated privately between two counterparties [fact-02].
3. Hedging a foreign payable locks in domestic costs by multiplying the payable by the forward offer rate [fact-03].
4. Hedging a foreign receivable locks in domestic proceeds by multiplying the receivable by the forward bid rate [fact-04].
5. Operating at 31:1 leverage exposes institutions to complete equity wipeout from a mere 3% to 4% asset decline [fact-05].
6. Default by a single leveraged institution can create systemic risk through cascading counterparty failure chains [fact-07].
7. The OTC derivatives market reached $630 trillion in principal and $21 trillion in gross market value by December 2014 [fact-08].
8. Post-2008 reforms mandate trading on SEFs, clearing through CCPs, and reporting to trade repositories [fact-06].
bottomTakeaway: Mastering derivatives requires understanding contract standardization, precise hedging via bid/offer rates, and how post-crisis CCP clearing mitigates catastrophic systemic leverage.
